The platform's paper channel is `pdf_print` — it RENDERS the letter; who franks and posts it is an integration nobody has chosen (BR-NOT-013: no adapter on any channel, print included).

no_dispatcher_reason: In-app messages are delivered today — they arrive in the bell straight away. Print, email and text messages are written and queued and you can read every one of them here, but sending is not switched on yet, so none of them leaves the building. Switching a rule on for one of those three decides what will be queued when sending arrives.
delivery_counts_reason: Nobody is reporting these back to us yet, because sending is not switched on. A zero here would look like every message had failed, which is not what is happening.

writer_reached_without_rule.dunning: notifications.notices.generate_reminder resolves it (BR-NOT-008's two reminder stages). The `past_due_reminder` event offers email and SMS and has no print switch, so no rule governs this printed class — but a writer does send it.
writer_reached_without_rule.receipt: apps.payments.receipts pins it by code when a payment is recorded. The `payment_received` event offers email only, so this printed receipt is outside every rule and inside a live flow.
writer_reached_without_rule.disconnect_notice_5_day: notifications.notices.generate_disconnect_notice resolves it through TIER_TO_CLASS at BR-NOT-014's second tier. The `disconnect_notice` event names the first tier's class, and one event rules the ladder.
writer_reached_without_rule.disconnect_notice_48_hour: the same writer at BR-NOT-014's final tier — see the entry above.
writer_reached_without_rule.account_message: customers.communication_api.account_communication queues it — the Communication dialog on an account (ACC-S16). The writer is a CLERK and not a flow, so no SET-12 rule governs it and none should: a utility may not switch off its own staff's typing.
